newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran hangs three for dealing in drugs.
newsitem.headline: Iran hangs three for dealing in drugs.

text.p: Iran has hanged three men in the western city of Khorramabad for dealing in drugs, a newspaper said on Saturday.
The Hamshahri daily said the three convicted drug offenders were hanged in a detention camp for drug addicts in Khorramabad, 570 km (360 miles) southwest of Tehran.
The report said the men were arrested last year for buying and selling illegal drugs. The sentence was carried out after Iran's supreme court confirmed the death sentence issued by a local court.
In a separate report the daily said Iranian police had seized 700 kg (1,543 lb) of opium over the past few days in three provinces.

Possession of 30 grams (just over an ounce) of heroin or five kg (11 lb) of opium is punishable by death under Iranian law. More than 1,000 people have been executed in drug-related cases since the law took effect in 1989.
Iran has an estimated one million drug addicts and is a key transit route for drugs, mostly opium, smuggled to Europe through Afghanistan and Pakistan -- the so-called "Golden Crescent".
